# Feed

> A list of articles that grows as the user scrolls, like a timeline. Page Down and Page Up move between articles, and a screenreader hears where each one is.

`<slab-feed>` · Data · built on `[role=feed] + <article>s`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/feed/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/feed.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-feed label="Updates" total="-1">
  <article>
    <h2>Forms set</h2>
    <p>…</p>
  </article>
  <article>
    <h2>Pour finished</h2>
    <p>…</p>
  </article>
</slab-feed>
```

Each child is an article. Feed puts it in the tab sequence, gives it `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, and names it by its first heading, so a screenreader says "Pour finished, 2 of 3" as focus lands on it. An article that isn't an `<article>` becomes a `[role=article]`, and one with a name or a role of its own keeps it.

Loading is yours. Append articles as the user nears the end, such as when an `IntersectionObserver` sees the last one, and set `busy` while you do, so a screenreader waits until they're in rather than reading half a page. Set `total` to how many articles there are in all, or -1 when you don't know, as in an endless timeline. Unset, it's the number of articles there are now.

## Keyboard

| Key                       | What it does                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Tab                       | Moves to each article, then through the links and buttons in it.                                 |
| Page Down, Page Up        | From anywhere in an article, moves to the next or previous article. Past either end, it scrolls. |
| Control+End, Control+Home | Moves focus out of the feed, to the first thing after it or the last thing before it.            |

## Elements

### `<slab-feed>`

Import `slab-elements/feed.js` to register it.

A feed with no visual styles, following the APG feed pattern: a list of articles that grows as the user scrolls, such as a timeline or a page of search results that loads more at the end.

Each slotted element is an article. It's put in the tab sequence and given `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, so a screenreader says where it is in the feed. It's a `[role=article]` unless it's an `<article>` or has a role of its own, and it's named by its first heading unless it has a name of its own.

Page Down and Page Up move focus to the next and previous article, from anywhere in one, so a keyboard user can skip through the feed without tabbing through each article's links. Control+End and Control+Home move focus out of the feed, to what's after and before it.

Loading is yours. Add articles to the end, or the start, and set `busy` while you do, so a screenreader waits until they're in. `total` is how many articles there are in all, when you know, or -1 when you don't, and the number of articles there are now when it's unset.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `busy`             | `boolean` | `false` | Articles are being added or removed. A screenreader waits until it's unset.                                                |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names the feed.                                                                                                            |
| `total`            | `number`  |         | How many articles there are in all, including those not added yet, or -1 when that's unknown. The number added when unset. |

#### Properties

| Name                | Type        | Description               |
| ------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
| `items` (read-only) | `Element[]` | Its Feed Items, in order. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type      | Description  |
| --------- | --------- | ------------ |
| (default) | `Element` | The articles |

#### CSS parts

| Name   | Description  |
| ------ | ------------ |
| `feed` | The articles |
